diagnosis.incident_summary: Order completion has been down 80% since 09:14 UTC after an unapproved APIM policy change at 09:12 tightened JWT audience validation and pricing-svc kept sending the old audience claim; only cached-price checkouts still complete.

timeline.description: CHG0044219 (normal): APIM policy revision 47, tighten JWT audience validation on internal service-to-service routes, deployed via release pipeline, no approval record
checkout confirmed using cached price data (pricing cache hit, no live APIM call) — these orders keep completing throughout the incident
order-orchestrator request timeout waiting on pricing-svc, retry exhaustion after 3 attempts
order.enriched producer rate collapses to near zero (lag=1, almost nothing new being produced)
order completion rate down 80% vs 15-min rolling baseline
INC0098470: Order flow degraded — pricing-svc auth failures

hypotheses.cause: APIM policy change CHG0044219 (revision 47) tightened JWT audience validation; pricing-svc still mints the old audience claim, so its calls are rejected

supports.why: A policy revision touching internal service-to-service auth deployed at 09:12, two minutes before the first 401, with no approval record on file.
The 401s are scoped to exactly one endpoint, /internal/pricing/quote — the one route the new audience-validation policy would affect if only one service sends the old claim.
order-orchestrator's timeout is specifically 'waiting on pricing-svc' — the failure is isolated to the pricing dependency, not a general network problem.
Order completion rate drops in lockstep with the 401 onset, with no other change event in this window.

contradicts.why: Checkout keeps completing successfully for cached-price items throughout the incident — on its face this makes the failure look partial and intermittent rather than a clean break in one dependency, which is why it took time to isolate: cached-price orders simply never call the broken APIM route.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: If cached-price checkouts also started failing (which never call APIM), that would rule out a scoped auth break and point at something upstream of the pricing cache instead.

hypotheses.cause: Flaky pricing-svc dependency, intermittent at the network level

supports.why: A generic timeout-and-retry-exhaustion message is superficially consistent with network flakiness.

contradicts.why: The failures are a clean, consistent 401 Unauthorized, not a mix of timeouts and connection errors — a flaky network path would not produce one uniform auth rejection code.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: A mix of error codes (timeouts, 5xx, connection resets) rather than a uniform 401 would support genuine network flakiness instead.

ruled_out.reason: Different service (nightly-settlement-batch), no shared correlation ID with the pricing/APIM chain, resolved before the incident began.
Same unrelated nightly-settlement-batch job; timing overlap with the incident window is coincidental.

checks.action: Diff the APIM policy XML for revision 47 against revision 46
checks.command: az apim api-revision list --service-name meridian-apim --api-id internal-pricing && diff revision46.xml revision47.xml
checks.if_result_a: expected_audience claim changed — confirms the policy is the trigger
checks.if_result_b: No audience-related change — reopens the investigation

checks.action: Decode a rejected pricing-svc JWT and compare its audience claim to the new policy's expected value
checks.if_result_a: Token audience does not match the new expected_audience — confirms hypothesis 1 exactly
checks.if_result_b: Audience matches — points away from the policy change entirely

checks.action: Check the change record's approval trail for CHG0044219
checks.if_result_a: No approval on file — supports an unreviewed/rushed deploy as a contributing factor
checks.if_result_b: Approved with sign-off — deploy process is not itself a contributing factor

recovery.proposal: Roll back APIM policy revision 47 to revision 46 to restore the previous audience validation immediately; separately, issue pricing-svc a token that mints the new 'meridian-internal-v2' audience claim so revision 47 can be safely redeployed once pricing-svc is updated.
recovery.risk: Rolling back the policy also reverts the security tightening it was meant to provide for every other internal caller, not just pricing-svc, until the forward fix is redeployed.
recovery.rollback: Re-apply revision 47 if the revision-46 rollback causes unexpected issues elsewhere; no data is mutated by either policy version, only request-time validation behaviour.

diagnosis.post_incident_note: INC0098470 — root cause: unapproved APIM policy revision 47 (CHG0044219) tightened JWT audience validation on internal routes; pricing-svc continued minting the old audience claim, causing all live-price checkouts to fail auth from 09:14. Cached-price checkouts were unaffected, which delayed detection. Mitigated via policy rollback to revision 46 once approved. Follow-up: require approval gates on APIM policy changes touching shared internal routes, and add a contract test that fails CI if a service's token audience drifts from the policy's expected value.

diff.changed_summary: The policy diff confirms the exact mechanism: revision 47 changed expected_audience from 'meridian-internal' to 'meridian-internal-v2', and pricing-svc's token issuer was never updated to match — this closes the one open question against hypothesis 1 and removes any remaining basis for the flaky-dependency alternative.

what_changed: The revision 47 diff shows expected_audience literally changed from 'meridian-internal' to 'meridian-internal-v2' — the exact claim mismatch predicted by hypothesis 1, now confirmed rather than inferred from timing alone.

pricing-svc's token issuer configuration was never updated to mint the new audience — this identifies precisely which side of the contract broke, sharpening the recovery proposal from 'roll back the policy' to 'roll back, then fix the issuer config before redeploying revision 47'.
